revenueEbitda.title: Revenue vs EBITDA
revenueEbitda.content:
Revenue is total group gaming and non-gaming income across SkyCity's four casino precincts (Auckland, Adelaide, Hamilton, Queenstown) plus the small Online segment. EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation — the operating profit measure before SkyCity's heavy fixed-cost base of debt service and depreciation on its precincts.

For SkyCity: revenue is essentially FLAT over the decade (FY2016 $998.7m → FY2026 $813.7m) while EBITDA has nearly halved (FY2018 $338.7m → FY2026 $120.5m). High operating leverage means small revenue swings produce large EBITDA swings — the mechanism behind the collapse.

What to watch:

  • Whether cost-out ($30m FY27, $70m FY28 target) and the NZICC ramp can lift EBITDA off this base without a revenue recovery
  • Carded Play's estimated $20-30m FY26 EBITDA drag — is it a one-off reset or a permanently lower base?
  • Log scale is on: this chart mixes very different EBITDA years, so a log axis shows the proportional collapse better than a linear one

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin
ebitdaMargin.content:
EBITDA as a percentage of revenue. Because SkyCity's licences, precincts and staff base are largely fixed costs, this ratio is the single best summary of how much of each revenue dollar the business keeps.

For SkyCity: margin fell from 33.4% in FY2016 to 14.8% in FY2026, driven by carded play, host-responsibility and AML compliance cost inflation, and the Adelaide remediation programme — not by a single event. The DCF's base case assumes a recovery only to ~24% by year 4, still well below the historical level.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin stabilises around FY26's ~15% or continues to erode as B3 Adelaide costs rise further before rolling off in FY28
  • Any signal the ~$20-30m Carded Play EBITDA drag is temporary rather than structural

netIncome.title: Net Income & Net Margin
netIncome.content:
Reported net profit after tax and the resulting net margin.

For SkyCity: FY2026's reported NPAT of $18.2m is NOT a genuine earnings recovery — pre-tax income was a LOSS of $12.1m, and the reported profit exists only because of a $30.3m income tax benefit. The DCF explicitly excludes P/E as a valuation anchor for this reason. FY2024's -$143.3m reflects a large impairment.

What to watch:

  • Whether pre-tax income (not the tax-affected headline number) turns durably positive
  • One-off items: impairments (FY2024, FY2026 Adelaide CGU), tax benefits, and non-cash FX translation reserve releases distort this line most years

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow, CapEx & Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Operating cash flow less capital expenditure. SkyCity's OCF excludes interest (presented in financing activities), so this is an unlevered free cash flow view, consistent with the DCF's own basis.

For SkyCity: FCF was negative in FY2019, FY2020 (COVID), FY2022, FY2024 and FY2025 — five of the last eight fiscal years — driven by heavy precinct capex (including the $750m NZICC) against a shrinking EBITDA base. FY2026 FCF was barely positive at $8.0m. No log toggle is offered on this chart because the series crosses zero.

What to watch:

  • Whether FCF turns durably positive as NZICC capex tapers and cost-out benefits land
  • Capex intensity: the DCF assumes it steps down from ~11% to ~10% of revenue as the convention centre build cycle ends

netDebt.title: Total Debt vs Cash
netDebt.content:
Gross borrowings and lease liabilities against cash on hand. The DCF nets these (plus a haircut on non-operating assets) into the equity bridge.

For SkyCity: total debt has grown from $427.1m (FY2016) to $719.3m (FY2026) against a materially SMALLER EBITDA base, pushing net debt/underlying EBITDA to 3.1x at FY26 year-end — above the ~3.75x historical covenant ceiling with limited headroom. Management guides this below 2.0x in FY27, contingent on completing $275-300m of asset sales.

What to watch:

  • Execution of the asset monetisation programme — the Auckland car park concession process already failed to attract an acceptable offer
  • Credit rating (currently BBB- at S&P) and covenant headroom

bookValue.title: Shareholders' Equity (Book Value)
bookValue.content:
Total shareholders' equity per the balance sheet — the accounting net asset value of the group.

For SkyCity: FY2026 equity rose to $1,545.0m, but this is entirely a function of the ~$229m August 2025 capital raise; organic equity actually FELL by $14.4m, and book value per share dropped 20.1% (to $1.401) on the enlarged share count. The stock trades at 0.48x this book value versus a 10-year median of 1.24x and an all-time low of 0.42x set this year — the DCF's book-value cross-check argues the asset story currently supports the price better than the earnings story does.

What to watch:

  • Whether book value stabilises as impairments (Adelaide CGU, -$62.4m FY2026) taper
  • Realisation of the $275-300m asset monetisation programme against carrying value

shares.title: Shares Outstanding
shares.content:
Total ordinary shares on issue at each fiscal year end (or, for FY2026, the weighted average used in the CSV/EPS — see annotation for the higher actual count).

For SkyCity: the August 2025 capital raise (NZ$240m at 70 cents/share, a ~30% discount) lifted the weighted-average FY2026 count to 1,037.1m from FY2025's 759.2m (+37%), and the actual count on issue reached 1,103.1m by August 2026 (+45% vs FY2025). The DCF values per-share using the higher, current 1,103.1m figure, not the lower weighted average, to avoid overstating intrinsic value.

What to watch:

  • No further dilution is currently planned; stock-based comp is negligible (0.09% of revenue)
  • Any per-share comparison spanning FY2025-FY2026 must account for this step change
